Plot functional pathway profiles

Source: R/mp_function.R
mp_function.Rd

Visualises functional-prediction tables such as PICRUSt2 pathway abundances or HUMAnN pathway/gene-family tables. Accepts either a phyloseq::phyloseq object (whose "taxa" are pathways) or a plain features-by-samples matrix / data frame plus optional sample metadata.

Usage

mp_function(
  object,
  metadata = NULL,
  plot.type = c("heatmap", "bar", "bubble"),
  group.by = NULL,
  top.n = 25,
  category = NULL,
  relative = TRUE,
  scale = c("none", "row"),
  palette = NULL,
  theme = NULL,
  plot.title = NULL,
  plot.subtitle = NULL,
  plot.caption = NULL,
  font.size = getOption("micropubr.font.size", 11),
  interactive = FALSE,
  verbose = getOption("micropubr.verbose", FALSE)
)

Arguments

object

A phyloseq::phyloseq object, or a matrix / data frame with pathways in rows and samples in columns.

metadata

Optional sample metadata data frame (rows = samples) used when object is a matrix.

plot.type

One of "heatmap", "bar" or "bubble".

group.by

Sample metadata column used to facet / summarise.

top.n

Number of most-abundant pathways to display.

category

Optional column (when object carries feature metadata, or a named vector) grouping pathways into higher-level categories for the bar plot (e.g. KEGG level 1/2).

relative

Convert to per-sample relative abundance.

scale

Row scaling for the heatmap: "none" or "row" (z-score).

palette

Palette name or colour vector.

theme

A ggplot2 theme; defaults to mp_theme_publication().

plot.title, plot.subtitle, plot.caption

Optional labels.

font.size

Base font size.

interactive

If TRUE, return an interactive plotly widget instead of a static ggplot (requires plotly). See mp_alpha().

verbose

Print the steps used.

Value

A ggplot object, or a plotly widget when interactive = TRUE.

Examples

set.seed(1)
m <- matrix(rpois(20 * 12, 50), nrow = 20,
            dimnames = list(paste0("path", 1:20), paste0("S", 1:12)))
meta <- data.frame(Group = rep(c("A", "B"), each = 6),
                   row.names = colnames(m))
mp_function(m, metadata = meta, plot.type = "heatmap", group.by = "Group")
